findings.issue: Cyrus's 'There are peanuts in all the food on this counter' overstates the review. Slate Window review 2 lists lentil soup, steamed greens, a chickpea stew and a quinoa salad with no peanuts, and Brooke's next line names only the grain bowls and granola. findings.where: venue downtown_linden_corner review 2, downtown_wren_house review 2, downtown_marble_steps review 2
findings.issue: The roll-call template is gone, but the rewrite added a new shared shape. Three safe-attribute reviews each list ingredient swaps (oat by default, olive oil instead of butter, white beans for silkiness / pumpkin seeds for crunch, herby oil where you'd expect crème fraîche / flour-and-water batter, syrup rather than butter, no milk jug). Each one is fair and evidences its venue, but side by side they read like the 'repeated checklists' map-seeder v6 asks to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Shorten one of them to a single experiential detail, e.g. Marble Steps review 2: '...and fritters crowd the plate, all fried in sunflower oil. My sister, who's badly allergic to peanuts and can't have dairy either, picks this place for her birthday brunch every year with zero worry.'

summary: Re-review after the human edits, narrative-writer v5 and map-seeder v6. Earlier suggestions 1-8 are all resolved. 'Sushi day' is now a bible Callback. Cyrus's vegetarian line is the new 'Then sushi day is today's standard.' Linden Corner lists five meat-free dishes. The multi-person roll calls are gone. Wren House rules out a bake case. Slate Window's fail lines now point to the satay bowls and granola. Mina's line has the bone broth. Cyrus has a new fail shape. Nothing regressed. Every scored constraint is still findable in implied style. Mina never states her diet, and the vegetarian clue is still carried by Roxy's 'whole section with zero meat in it', Mina's 'without asking about any of it' and Cyrus's 'standard', as clue rule 1 requires. Every review still evidences its venue's deciding attributes. Wren House's peanut safety ('haven't spotted a nut on the premises', seed crunch, plain dressings) is a firsthand observation, enough for an implied level, and it isn't the attribute that decides Wren's score. All outcome lines now match the rewritten reviews. What's left is polish: Cyrus's 'all the food' overstatement, a new ingredient-swap checklist shared by three reviews, and mixed regional words.
